A1.justification: Both readable 30-page PDFs describe the same Rec-R1 work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original product-search and sequential-recommendation experiments, generalization evaluations, ablations, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3, the generalization evaluations, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Rec-R1 retains the same closed-loop optimization of LLM-generated text using black-box recommendation feedback and GRPO. The objectives, components, and task-specific procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ESCI, Amazon-C4, Amazon Beauty, MMLU, IFEval, GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval. Product domains, cross-domain search coverage, and transductive/inductive recommendation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments. Table 2 retains GPT-4o+BM25 and Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct+BM25; only their scores change.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, checkpoint selection, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix E. No protocol revision accompanies the Table 2 score replacements.

E4.justification: The prompt-style analysis, reasoning/JSON ablations, forgetting evaluation, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged in Table 7, Tables 9–10, Figure 3, and Appendix G. No diagnostic experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Two baseline rows change in Table 2 under unchanged reported Amazon-C4 NDCG@100 settings. In Video Games, Baby, Office, and Sports order, GPT-4o+BM25 changes from 9.20/8.68/8.81/8.51 to 13.02/12.45/12.64/11.59; Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct+BM25 changes from 5.96/5.17/6.62/6.39 to 10.33/8.62/9.61/9.05. Qwen+BM25 now exceeds plain BM25 in every domain, narrowing Rec-R1's advantage. Rec-R1 scores and all other results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Theorem 1 and its assumptions, and the lemma and proofs in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about direct recommendation-feedback optimization, performance advantages, and preservation of general LLM capabilities.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the discussion of prompting, inductive versus transductive performance, and Appendix F's applicability boundaries. Section 3.1.2 is not revised to reflect the higher sparse-prompting baseline scores.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's first-page footnote providing the Rec-R1 code repository link, without replacing it elsewhere. Implementation settings and the VeRL library reference remain. This removes access information; it does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix B's comparisons with previous LLM recommendation and reinforcement-learning approaches.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to deleting the code footnote, renumbering the remaining footnote, and updating the arXiv version/date text. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Footnote removal and renumbering produce minor spacing and text-placement changes. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–10 retain their structure and placement; Table 2 changes only numerical entries.

improvement.justification: v2 removes the project's code-access link, reducing reproducibility information. Its higher sparse-prompting scores also make Section 3.1.2's unchanged description of negligible improvements or degradation less representative. Rec-R1 still leads and the scientific contribution remains intact, so these reporting regressions constitute a limited overall decline.
